protocol.description:
WinFusion private protocol for sharing AHardwareBuffers with the compositor. A buffer is always transferred as a serialized AHardwareBuffer handle written to a unix socket, preceded by a small layout header. Both allocation directions are supported:
- create_buffer: the compositor allocates the AHardwareBuffer and writes its handle into the socket supplied by the client.
- import_buffer (since version 2): an Android-side process allocates the AHardwareBuffer, writes its handle into a socketpair, and the client relays the peer end of that socketpair to the compositor, which deserializes the handle.
In both cases the client process itself never has to load Android private libraries: it either consumes the dma-buf fds of the handle, or it merely forwards a socket file descriptor it received out-of-band.
Either way the compositor ends up importing the buffer as an EGLImage, so compositing samples the very gralloc allocation the producer rendered into.
This is the Android equivalent of zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1: it exists because Android EGL does not expose EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import.

interface.name: zwp_winfusion_buffer_v1
interface.description: This global provides a way to create wl_buffer objects backed by AHardwareBuffers shared through a socket, either allocated by the compositor (create_buffer) or by an Android-side producer (import_buffer).

request.name: create_buffer

description.summary: create a buffer backed by an AHardwareBuffer

request.description:
Creates a wl_buffer backed by an AHardwareBuffer.
The compositor allocates an AHardwareBuffer compatible with the requested geometry and format, then writes a small layout header and the serialized AHardwareBuffer handle to socket_fd. The client imports the first dma-buf fd from that handle into Vulkan.
The format argument is the DRM fourcc of the buffer contents as read by the compositor.

arg.name: socket_fd
arg.summary: socket used for the server reply

request.name: import_buffer

description.summary: import a buffer backed by an externally allocated AHardwareBuffer

request.description:
Creates a wl_buffer from an AHardwareBuffer that was allocated outside of the compositor.
The request direction is client to compositor, but the client is not the writer of socket_fd. The AHardwareBuffer is allocated and serialized by the Android-side renderer, which creates a socketpair, writes the layout header followed by the serialized handle (AHardwareBuffer_sendHandleToUnixSocket) into one end, and hands the peer end to the client out-of-band. The client only relays that file descriptor here; it never parses or reconstructs the handle, so it does not need Android private libraries.
The compositor reads the layout header, then recovers the AHardwareBuffer with AHardwareBuffer_recvHandleFromUnixSocket. The header fields must agree with the width, height and format arguments of this request, and the recovered buffer must match the requested geometry and format; otherwise this is a protocol error.
The format argument is the DRM fourcc of the buffer contents.

arg.name: socket_fd
arg.summary: socket carrying the serialized AHardwareBuffer handle
